title: Choose MarkDN's iPad and iPhone world
question: The roll assigned the card catalogue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Card Catalogue
options.lineage: library card catalogues: oak drawers, typed index cards, tabbed guide cards, date-due stamps
options.thesis: Every document is a card in a drawer: the drawer is your folder, the card is the page.
options.viewport: iPad landscape: an oak drawer of card edges on the left with folder guide-tabs, the open card across the rest, its title on the red top rule, source and render side by side.
options.risk: Card stock and a red rule sit near the warm-paper cliché; it holds only if the oak shell and blue ruling carry the colour, never cream alone.

raised.raise: Palette held to six named inks; greys exist only as ink at set opacities.
The drawer opens as a whole-cell grid of cards, each card's state (open, edited, agent-touched) marked in one fixed corner cell.
All chrome at one size; rank is carried by weight and case, never by scaling labels.
Every card keeps the index card's 5:3 proportion and one shared baseline in both panes.
One 8px rhythm; hairlines do all the division, no shadows anywhere.

options.label: Pocket Paperbacks
options.lineage: Penguin paperbacks and Tschichold's tripartite cover grid
options.thesis: Each folder is a paperback series: colour bands by folder, documents read like a pocket book on iPhone.
options.viewport: iPad landscape: a shelf of folder-coloured spines on the left, the open document under a three-band title (series colour, white title band, series colour), source and render below.
options.risk: Familiar bookish nostalgia, and the direction most runs in this category land on; heavy orange chrome can fight the document.

options.label: Midnight Line
options.lineage: a metropolitan rail map fired as midnight-blue enamel
options.thesis: The document is a line: headings are stations, your scroll is the train, folders are coloured lines.
options.viewport: iPad landscape: the outline as a vertical line with station ticks on the left, the current section a lit interchange; the document on porcelain to the right.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the outline-as-line is a better touch navigator than a sync rail; loses audience identification, since writers think in documents, not journeys.
options.risk: A midnight ground is heavy behind long reading, and the map turns decorative if the line is not the real navigator.

options.label: Plate Section
options.lineage: a design annual's plate section on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Documents as plates in an annual, registered to a hairline grid.
options.viewport: A sheet of document plates with mono credits rows.
options.case: Fuses thin: reads as a designers' annual, not a writer's editor; loses both axes.
options.kept: One 8px rhythm with hairlines doing all division.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.lineage: a 1971 pocket airline timetable on a lit goldenrod bed
options.thesis: Everything at one type size, rank carried by weight and case.
options.viewport: A raked rack of document slides read laterally.
options.case: Fuses poorly: one size for prose and headings breaks markdown's own hierarchy; loses both axes.
options.risk: Raked containers fight reading on a phone.
options.kept: All chrome at one size; rank by weight and case.

options.label: Circle Catalogue
options.lineage: a convention circle catalog on newsprint
options.thesis: Every document a stamp-sized cell, circled in biro when visited.
options.viewport: A packed grid of document thumbnails keyed to a folder map.
options.case: Fuses partially: the grid is a fine iPad home, but the audience has no tie to it; loses both axes.
options.risk: Thumbnails of text documents read as noise.
options.kept: A whole-cell document grid with state marked in one fixed cell.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: a botanical folio of one plant across a season
options.thesis: A document's history as plates at one fixed scale.
options.viewport: Versions of a document banded on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses thin: MarkDN has no version timeline to show; loses both axes.
options.risk: Cream and engraved italics sit in the warm-paper cluster.
options.kept: A fixed card proportion and one shared baseline.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The document as a strobing data field in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A barcode field with the document set as dense tabular mono.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing fields are hostile to hours of reading; loses both axes.
options.kept: A palette held to a few named inks, no in-between greys.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An iPadOS document app as Apple ships them: sidebar, document, system colours.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of documents, the document with a large title, toolbar of system controls.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Notes and every markdown app by design.
